title: pausing a session, and the row that says so
asserts: a core that advertises `sessionSleep` lets a client put a session to sleep on purpose, and leaves behind a row that is distinguishable from a kill. The flag lands on the wire BEFORE the pty dies - a `sessionMeta` carrying `dormant: true`, then the `exit` - so the exited row the death finalises reads "slept, wake me on demand" rather than "died"; the core's OWN snapshot says the same thing, which is the half a client cannot supply for itself and the whole reason the frame exists (the desktop's global pause used to send a plain `kill` and write `dormant` onto its private mirror row, so the core, its reaper and its boot-time rehydrate all saw five paused agents as five ended ones - juancode-nizo); a `reactivate` wakes exactly the session it names and clears only that flag, leaving the rest of the paused set asleep, which is what makes "play brings back what pause took" a promise rather than a hope; and a session whose pty is already gone is refused with an `error` instead of flagged, because a crash relabelled as asleep is a row a global play would wake as if somebody had paused it.

steps.note: two sessions, because half of what a pause promises is about the one it did NOT wake
the flag first, while the pty is still alive. Flagging after the kill leaves an exited row that every client renders as a crash, which is the one thing dormant exists to prevent
and only then is the CLI process tree freed, which is the point of pausing rather than leaving it running
asked again, now that the pty is gone
refused, not flagged a second time. A row that already says asleep must not be the answer to every later ask either: the interesting case is the one below, where a row that never slept must not start
the daemon's own snapshot, which is the whole difference from a flag a client wrote into its private mirror
exited AND dormant, in the core's own list: this is what a restore plan and a liveness accounting read, and with a plain kill both of them read "ended"
asked again, because the assertion below is about the other session
one wake and the moon clears; waking is reactivate and deliberately has no frame of its own
exactly the one that was woken. The second clause is the "exactly": no row for the session nobody woke may claim it is awake, or a play after a pause brings back sessions the pause never took
this scenario's own cleanup: it woke a session, so it ends it
